title: Holding, Radial Intercept, Bearing to Plot
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 6. Most are the book's worked examples turned into choices (answer = the book's working); Q5, 16, 18–20, 31–33 keyed from the printed grid, PDF p. 269

o: fly to the NDB and join the pattern
fly to the NDB, then a teardrop with an outbound heading of 120° for 1 minute and a rate-one turn to join inbound
fly to the NDB, then outbound on 150° for 1 minute, then turn left to point at the NDB, joining overhead

o: 030°(M) Ans. MBT / MBF = 040°/220° MH = 040° Final MBT/MBF = 150/330° Intercept Angle = 040° New MH = 330° + 040° = 370° - 360° = 010 HOLDING, RADIAL INTERCEPT, BEARING TO PLOT

ex.1: Book: sector 2 runs 145° to 075° (radial), the aircraft on 140 is in it: offset (teardrop).
ex.2: MBT = 150 + 10 = 160, aircraft on radial 340: sector 1, parallel.
ex.3: MBT = 060 − 10 = 050, aircraft on radial 230: sector 2, offset.
ex.7: Outbound 090°: the wind from 130° gives about 19–20 kt headwind; add 1 s per knot: about 80 s.
ex.8: Drift 8° on the legs; outbound apply 3 × drift: 030 − 24 = 006. GS out 193 kt: 13 kt tailwind → 60 − 13 = 47 s.
ex.9: Difference 20° → double = 40, round up to 60°. Heading 070 + 60 = 130; RB = 070 − 130 + 360 = 300.
ex.15: MBT 120 → final 090; 60° intercept: 150; RB = 090 − 150 + 360 = 300. The book then joins the 110 non-standard hold with a parallel entry.
ex.17: MBT 235 → final 255; 60° intercept: 255 − 60 = 195 (turn left 30°; ADF 060 at the intercept).
ex.18: At the intercept the heading is 120 − 50 = 070; RB = 120 − 070 = 050.
ex.21: QUJ = 173 + 3 (VOR variation) = 176; QTE = 356; on a Lambert chart BTP = QTE.
ex.31: Inbound on 210 radial = track 030; intercept 30°: 060; RB = 030 − 060 + 360 = 330.
